did_you_know.text: The Lord left certain nations in the land to test Israel and see whether they would keep his commandments, and also to teach the generations who had not known the wars in Canaan.
Among the nations left in the land were the five rulers of the Philistines, the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in the mountains of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
The Israelites married the people living among them and also served their gods; this is how Scripture describes the danger of living among the nations of Canaan.
After they served the Baals and the Asherahs, the Israelites were handed over to Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram-naharaim, for eight years.
Othniel son of Kenaz delivered Israel after the Spirit of the Lord came upon him. Following his victory, the land had peace for forty years.
Eglon king of Moab joined forces with the Ammonites and Amalekites, defeated Israel, and took possession of the City of Palms; the Israelites served him for eighteen years.
Ehud son of Gera made a double-edged sword a gomed long and strapped it under his clothes against his right thigh.
Ehud drew the sword with his left hand—Scripture describes him as left-handed—and used it to kill Eglon king of Moab.
After escaping, Ehud blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites seized the Jordan crossings to prevent the Moabites from crossing.
Shamgar son of Anath struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad, and Scripture also presents him as a deliverer of Israel.
